alternatives.option: Continue the exact candidate stack into host-neutral BH-02 contract design
alternatives.rationale: Active semantics, isolation, recovery, and reproducibility pass while known failures have bounded conditions.
alternatives.revisit_trigger: Any active stop condition becomes triggered.

alternatives.option: Replace AtomVM or Popcorn before BH-02
alternatives.rationale: Immediate replacement is not justified by current active proofs, but runtime semantics, security, or build failure can trigger it.
alternatives.revisit_trigger: Runtime proof failure, unsafe bridge dead end, or unbounded resource behavior.

alternatives.option: Fork or patch a pinned dependency
alternatives.rationale: A fork adds maintenance burden and is justified only when an owned upstream limitation blocks a required proof or condition.
alternatives.revisit_trigger: Pinned upstream cannot satisfy a required bounded mitigation.

alternatives.rationale: Standalone DOM and Phoenix authority boundaries remain independent, so private API incompatibility need not block the core browser host.
alternatives.revisit_trigger: Private pins drift or adapter maintenance outweighs demonstrated value.

alternatives.option: Revise the profile through AVM pruning and actual compressed serving
alternatives.rationale: The current unpruned application bundle is the dominant payload and fails both active application limits.
alternatives.revisit_trigger: Before any release or production profile claim.

alternatives.option: Block and archive the candidate browser stack
alternatives.rationale: No active semantic, isolation, reproducibility, or accounting stop condition is triggered after bounded conditions are applied.
alternatives.revisit_trigger: A condition cannot be satisfied without violating neutral or authority boundaries.

conditions.expiry: Expires when superseded by accepted measured reachability evidence.
conditions.required_action: Run a sound module-reachability experiment with before/after manifests and repeat affected Phases 3–10 proofs.
conditions.trigger: Before release qualification or material bundle composition change

conditions.expiry: Expires when an accepted production-serving profile supersedes the local estimate.
conditions.required_action: Verify actual precompressed serving, negotiation, MIME, integrity, cache, isolation, proxy, and CDN behavior.
conditions.trigger: Before production profile deployment or transfer-size claim

conditions.expiry: Expires only on accepted same-boundary stable-product evidence.
conditions.required_action: Attribute harness/runtime phases, optimize without changing semantics, and repeat the same timer distribution in a stable Firefox product.
conditions.trigger: Before stable Firefox support or interaction-budget promotion

conditions.expiry: Reevaluated at every private dependency revision.
conditions.required_action: Repeat private-surface inventory and compatibility probes while retaining standalone DOM fallback and neutral package isolation.
conditions.trigger: Any Phoenix, LiveView, LocalLiveView, or optional adapter change

conditions.expiry: Reevaluated at every named runtime or toolchain change.
conditions.required_action: Repeat affected runtime, browser, behavior, resilience, measurement, and clean-rebuild proofs from immutable inputs.
conditions.trigger: Any runtime, OTP, Popcorn, toolchain, bridge, or canonical build-root change

conditions.expiry: Expires only through an accepted production security gate.
conditions.required_action: Design and validate production identity, TLS/proxy, persistence, distributed limits, CSP, audit, monitoring, and penetration-test controls.
conditions.trigger: Before production authentication, deployment, or security claim

conditions.expiry: Remains open until BH-22 qualification accepts or rejects each deferred row.
conditions.required_action: Execute non-substitutable platform, stable-browser, physical-device, mobile, and manual assistive-technology qualification.
conditions.trigger: BH-22 start or availability of representative external environments

conditions.expiry: Expires only when BH-02 accepts independently reviewed neutral contracts.
conditions.required_action: Derive neutral contracts from observable facts and prohibit BH-01 messages, DOM operations, Phoenix routes, and profile fixtures from becoming public APIs by default.
conditions.trigger: During BH-02 semantic, renderer, capability, effect, or resource contract design

conditions.expiry: Expires only through an accepted release gate.
conditions.required_action: Complete SBOM, license/notice, signing, source-map, reachability, production serving, rollback, provenance, and release invalidation gates.
conditions.trigger: Before package publication or release-readiness claim

decision.rationale: The active Linux evidence proves the candidate can support neutral framework exploration, clean rebuilding, bounded lifecycle behavior, isolated server authority, and disposable rendering experiments. Payload, Firefox timing, private API, production, release, and external qualification gaps remain explicit owned conditions rather than hidden passes.

challenges: The application AVM is far over both payload targets, mobile value is unknown, and no support range exists.
favorable_observations: Local state, forms, timers, DOM updates, fallback, and one server-authorized command work end to end.
lenses.scope: Whether the active Linux slice provides enough value to justify neutral framework work.

challenges: BH-01 messages and DOM operations are disposable and too implementation-specific to become public contracts.
favorable_observations: Standalone DOM, optional LiveView, Phoenix authority, runtime, and fixture ownership remain separated.
lenses.scope: Whether proven facts can inform neutral contracts without importing browser or Phoenix details.

alternatives_considered: replace or fork runtime when a trigger fails
challenges: Timer cancellation reports false, Popcorn requires unsafe-eval, and long-soak/fairness evidence remains incomplete.
favorable_observations: Boot, process/message behavior, recovery, generation isolation, and bounded cleanup pass repeated active scenarios.
lenses.scope: Whether AtomVM and Popcorn expose sufficient bounded process, message, timer, and lifecycle behavior.

challenges: The build is multi-language, path-sensitive without a canonical mount, and expensive enough to demand strict automation.
favorable_observations: Two clean contexts rebuild and exercise the whole baseline noninteractively with deterministic derived reports.
lenses.scope: Whether the build, host, bridge, profile, and evidence burden remains manageable for framework exploration.

challenges: High payload and private-API risk can still make later replacement, adapter removal, or a fork preferable.
favorable_observations: No active semantic or isolation stop condition is triggered, so immediate replacement would discard validated capability.
lenses.scope: Whether replacement, pinning, forking, adapter removal, profile revision, or blocking is more justified.

challenges: Production identity, TLS/proxy, persistence, distributed limits, CSP removal, audit sinks, and penetration testing are absent.
favorable_observations: Client claims are rejected, authority is server-owned, integrity drift fails before readiness, and retained diagnostics are redacted.
lenses.scope: Whether current trust, integrity, adversarial, diagnostics, and cleanup evidence is sufficient for BH-02 input.

challenges: No screen-reader pairing, physical mobile input, virtual keyboard, touch, rotation, or accessibility conformance review executed.
favorable_observations: Required fallback content and automated keyboard/focus/field observations pass in active development evidence.
lenses.scope: Whether automated fallback, keyboard, focus, names, roles, fields, and unavailable manual evidence are represented truthfully.

challenges: Only exact package pins and one Linux host are evidenced; Firefox is a development binary and Safari/mobile are absent.
favorable_observations: Active Chrome and Firefox development runs agree semantically; private mismatch disables the optional adapter.
lenses.scope: Whether browser prerequisites and private package surfaces have a bounded compatibility posture.

challenges: Payload and Firefox timer budgets fail; Chrome reruns drift; heap/process observations and long-soak methods are incomplete.
favorable_observations: Raw samples, unchanged thresholds, deterministic reports, failures, and representative reruns are retained.
lenses.scope: Whether measurement methods, negative outcomes, resource observations, and rerun variance support the decision.

challenges: AVM reachability is unpruned and actual Brotli negotiation, CDN/proxy behavior, production rollback, and SBOM release automation remain future work.
favorable_observations: Exact archives, locks, licenses, manifests, artifact hashes, source-map policy, and stale-artifact recovery are recorded.
lenses.scope: Whether artifact origin, reachability, licenses, integrity, maps, serving, rollback, and release gaps are visible.

challenges: Both authoritative contexts share one physical host and browser timings remain scheduler-sensitive observations.
favorable_observations: A/B authoritative runs agree exactly or semantically and all three failed attempts remain separate from the pass.
lenses.scope: Whether the final evidence is source-bound, reciprocal, reproducible, failure-preserving, and honest about scope.
